hypothesis: Batched GPU prefill for expert-pruned checkpoints (pr1) speeds up REAP-132 prefill over upstream, which refuses the GPU batch path for !=256 experts and runs the CPU union
model: DeepSeek V4 Flash REAP 150B (puwaer/DeepSeek-V4-Flash-0731-reap-150b, 132 routed experts, fp4 experts / fp8 dense), colibri safetensors layout, 79 GiB on disk
command: build: cd c && make -f Makefile.deepseek-v4 deepseek-v4 CUDA=1 CUDA_HOME=/usr NVCC=/usr/bin/nvcc CUDA_ARCH=sm_86 NO_TC=1; run: python3 c/coli serve --model <REAP dir> --ram 40 --ctx 8192 --host 127.0.0.1 --port 8090 with the env in config; one cold server per sample; client bench_pr1.py sends request 1 (1992-token prompt, max_tokens 100) then request 2 (3005-token prompt, max_tokens 60), streamed, greedy; tok_s = prompt_tokens / time-to-first-token of the named request; metric: request 'long_prefill'

hardware.cpu: AMD Ryzen 9 9950X3D, 16 cores / 32 threads, 1 socket (engine: 16 OpenMP compute threads + 3 expert-loader lanes)
hardware.ram: 62 GiB DDR5; engine --ram 40 (31.6 GiB routed-expert RAM cache, 6.2 GiB dense resident)
hardware.storage: WD_BLACK SN850X 4 TB NVMe (PCIe 4.0), ext4 root filesystem, model read with O_DIRECT (v4_ssd_io mode=direct-aligned)
hardware.os: Ubuntu 24.04.4 LTS, kernel 7.0.0-34-generic, gcc 13.3.0, CUDA toolkit 12.0.140 (generic build CUDA_ARCH=sm_86 NO_TC=1), NVIDIA driver 595.84; GPU0 NVIDIA GeForce RTX 3090 24 GB on PCIe 4.0 x8 (one GPU used)

quality.method: greedy (temperature 0): full output text of every request in every sample has the same sha256 as upstream dev (arm A); A itself identical across its 3 samples
